name: The Greyvasti

relationships.label: The Greyvasti originated in the city of Greyvast, the Sunken Throne — their entire civilization was built in the mist-choked coastal city before it was drowned.
The majority of the Greyvasti who survived Greyvast's fall became members of the Oathbound Remnants, carrying the memory of the dead into the new world.
The Hollow Covenant is the faith of the Greyvasti — their tradition of carving names into stone and reciting the dead is older than the Covenant itself.
A significant population of Greyvasti refugees fled to Ashenveil after Greyvast's fall — they carry their oral traditions in a city that does not mourn like they do.
The Greyvasti fear and revere Mourne the Hollow King as the collector of their unnumbered dead — every name carved is a soul they hope to save from his silence.

description: The Greyvasti are the original human inhabitants of Greyvast, a dying people who know they are dying. Gaunt, pale, with eyes that reflect moonlight even in total darkness, they are a culture defined by loss. Their civilization drowned with the Sunken Throne, and what remains is a people split between those who fight as Oathbound Remnants and those who fled as refugees to Ashenveil. Their tradition of oral memory preservation and oath-binding predates the Hollow Covenant, and every Greyvasti child learns to carve names into stone before they learn to write sentences.
excerpt: The original human inhabitants of Greyvast — a dying people with moon-touched eyes, an obsession with memory preservation, and a culture split between Remnants and refugees.
content:
The first thing you notice about a Greyvasti is their eyes. Even in absolute darkness — in the mist-choked streets of what remains of Greyvast, in the windowless halls of Mournwall, in the deepest corner of an Ashenveil tavern at midnight — their eyes catch light that should not exist. A faint, pale glow, like moonlight reflected off still water. The Greyvasti call it Yssara's Gift. Outsiders call it the mark of a dying people.

They are gaunt, uniformly so. Not from starvation — from generations of living in a city where the sun filtered through permanent mist, where the moon was the only reliable source of illumination. Their bodies adapted. Their skin is pale, almost translucent at the temples. Their fingers are long, built for carving — and carve they do, everywhere. Every stone in a Greyvasti settlement bears names. Doorframes. Hearthstones. The walls of refugee shelters in Ashenveil. The Name Wall at Mournwall is the most famous example, but any Greyvasti, presented with any stone, will begin to carve. It is involuntary. It is breathing.

Their oral tradition is ferocious. A Greyvasti child learns to recite their lineage back seven generations before they learn to read. The elders carry the entire history of Greyvast in their memories — every street name, every building, every family that lived in every house. When an elder dies, the Greyvasti hold a Wake of Memory that lasts three days. Every fact the elder carried is spoken aloud, recorded by the next generation, before it is permitted to fade.

But the people are splitting. Those who remained as Oathbound Remnants have turned their grief into a weapon — they carve names on Mournwall, swear oaths to Mourne, and fight to recover the bodies of the unrecovered. Those who fled to Ashenveil are building quiet lives in a city that does not share their grief. The refugees still carve names into their walls, but their children are learning Ashenveil's accent. The elders watch this and say nothing. They know what it means.

The Greyvasti are a dying people, and they know it. Their birth rate is low. Their eyes grow brighter with each generation, the moonlight in them more pronounced, as if Yssara is calling them home. They do not rage against this. They carve names. They tell stories. They wait.

name: The Pale-Touched

relationships.label: The Pale-Touched are created by prolonged exposure to Yssara's moon fragments — the silver glow in their veins is her power, consuming them from within.
The Pale Dominion venerates the Pale-Touched as living saints, parading them through the Pale Spire as evidence of Yssara's favor manifest in flesh.
The Doctrine of Controlled Erosion considers the Pale-Touched holy — they are the ultimate expression of sacred self-destruction, offering every fragment of their soul to Yssara.
Vel-Thara the Unmade feeds on the Pale-Touched — their accelerated soul erosion makes them a constant source of her corrupting influence and she claims them before their final breath.
The Oathbound Remnants fear and avoid the Pale-Touched, seeing them as the antithesis of oath-culture — what happens when you let the moon consume you instead of swearing to resist it.

description: The Pale-Touched are not a born race but a post-Fracture transformation — humans exposed to prolonged moon fragment radiation who slowly become something luminous and hollow. Their skin turns translucent, their veins glow faintly silver, and their soul accelerates toward complete erosion. The Pale Dominion venerates them as living saints. Everyone else treats them as a walking contagion. Most go fully mad within five years of transformation. They are weapons, oracles, and ticking existential clocks — often all three.
excerpt: Post-Fracture living saints — humans transformed by moon fragment exposure into luminous, hollow vessels. Venerated by the Dominion. Pitied by everyone else. Most go mad within five years.
content:
Stage One — First Exposure. The subject reports a persistent humming in their bones at night, as if a distant string had been plucked somewhere behind the sternum. Their eyes catch moonlight differently. Sleep becomes optional. The Dominion records the name of every newly touched subject. They are watched.

Stage Two — Translucence. The skin begins to thin. Not dramatically — a faint transparency at the temples, at the wrists, along the collarbone. Veins become visible beneath the surface, carrying a dull silver shimmer. The subject can see their own blood glowing in dim rooms. This is when most realize they will not recover.

Stage Three — The Bleed. Soul erosion accelerates beyond the body's ability to compensate. Emotions flatten. Memories develop gaps — not forgotten, but missing, as if pages were torn from a book. The subject becomes calm. Dangerously calm. The Dominion promotes them to sainthood at this stage. They are paraded through the Pale Spire in silver robes while the faithful weep at their passing.

Stage Four — Luminescence. The glow is active now. Veins burn silver-white under the skin, visible through clothing. Magical output triples, sometimes quadruples. The subject can cast spells that would kill an ordinary mage. They are at their most useful and their most dangerous. The Dominion confines them to ceremony. They are saints who must not be touched.

Stage Five — Cognitive Fray. Paranoia. Time distortion. The subject begins speaking to people who are not there — Yssara's voice, they claim. They forget faces, including their own reflection. They carve symbols into their own skin, trying to hold onto a self that is dissolving. The Dominion no longer parades them. They are kept below, in the lower chambers of the Pale Spire, where their light is still useful.

Stage Six — The Hollowing. The subject stops. No madness. No pain. No self. The body remains, animated by residual moon energy, but the person is gone — consumed entirely. The Pale-Touched call this the Silver Peace. The Oathbound Remnants call it death, and they mercy-kill any Hollowed they find. The Dominion calls it the final offering. All three are correct.

Most reach Stage Six within five years of Stage Two. Some faster. None have survived past it. The Pale-Touched do not reproduce — they are created, one exposure at a time, by a moon that will not stop falling.
